Knysna - the aftermath

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
300 Km of coast line burnt- 400 formal houses and 200 informal. 7 people have died including two elderly people. The economic heartland of the Eastern Cape is destroyed. Woodridge school destroyed sending children home from all over Africa. People's retirement investments destroyed. We follow up on the aftermath before the next storm hits on Thursday. Getting local footage of the the flames and drone footage. In one road 27 houses burnt out- communities shattered. Aid pouring in but how do you rebuild in a recession when everyone is already hard pressed

Press Release:


Knysna – The Aftermath
It has been a week since fires ravaged the town of Knysna and close to 300km of coastline, destroying more than 600 homes and buildings in its path. With nine people
dead, thousands left homeless and millions of rands in damages, residents have begun the arduous task of rebuilding their lives. Carte Blanche revisits the town to witness
how kind-hearted South Africans from all provinces are pulling together to assist those in need.

Script:


Link: “The smell of smoke still lingers in the air and the scale of the human tragedy along the coastline is almost impossible to reflect, everybody knows somebody who has lost everything. People seem to be in a daze trying to find a way forward
Ella Bauer: “When I got here it was horrendous, where ever you looked where ever you rode down the road things were just burning it was like a war zone
Script: 90 year old Erna Bauer and her daughter have returned to salvage her possession from her rented flat below the home of an elderly woman who lived upstairs.
Ella “The lady upstairs is 80 my mums 90 the lady upstairs completely as you can see behind us the house is completely finished she has no insurance
Erna Bauer “When I think about what I saw all that that was terrible
Script: Now like everyone else Erna needs to find a new home while the slow process of rebuilding over 700 homes begins.
Ella “So from here we take it day by day
Script: Many others are struggling to find accommodation and rentals have shot up across town
Script: This is all that’s left of Timber Village the indigenous furniture and wood factory , a major tourist feature of Knysna. It was the site of 3 business and several homes. Jock Mc Connachie employs 8 people and says his biggest loss is his irreplaceable treasure trove of rare woods
Jock “I haven’t really been able to formulate any plans yet it’s still too early but I would like to keep my guys employed because they are so good and they enjoy what they do
Script Kaamic Malindi has worked here for 17 years, he lost his home and workshop
Kaamic “We were so happy working here and this is what we were born to do I mean everybody liked it was their passion and their skill this was good for us
Derek Describe What happened on that day
Jock 14 27 09 07 We were all working they were in the workshop and I was in the office, my neighbour from across the road, he phoned me literally 5 minutes before we had to evacuate. We Couldn’t go back into the office couldn’t go back into the houses nothing we just jumped on the bakkie with embers flying across us
Kaamic “We have lost our work place but there is something that hasn’t burnt and that is our skill we ran with our skill”
Script: Kaamic lost 100 000 rands worth of his equipment from his private workshop. But their collegee Blessing Matope will never recover his loss. His 4 year old child and wife, where trapped in the fire a little further down the road while visiting friends
Kaamic “So it is just too much for a young man at his age he has lost his job because the place he has been working at has burnt down its too many loses for one person
Up Sound Derek greeting Blessing
Link: “Fire does not discriminate and losses have been massive throughout the entire community. Many have insurance but right here there is just no safety net
Script: Mercy Skosana escaped with her husband and 5 children and is staying with friends
Mercy “I really don’t k now what to do because I thought I was trying to extend my house so now I don’t know where to start
Derek “And how are your children coping
Mercy “They ask me how long are we going to stay in this house and I said ahh just wait so our hope is that the municipality can help us
Script: We returned to the Vineyard Church one of the many shelters around Knysna. At the start of the evacuation they accommodated patients from the local hospital
Dee-Ann Olivier “So Derek the last week which feels like 2 years has been incredible SA has been sending more and more supplies. So we were able to help a lot of people with immediate disaster relief..
Script: Systems are now in place with collect points closer to the victims
Link” Aid in many forms is pouring in from around the country, in around the world and going to small distribution centres like this one. The Western cape Government has pledged R75 million and there is hope there is more to come
Script: With the region officially declared a disaster area more funding has been made available for reconstruction. Executive Mayor Eleanor Bouw Spies reports back on the plans for housing
Mayor “People have been amazing from all over not only from Knysna have come in an offered their expertise to try and rebuild this town into something better…we have already had an initial meeting with business people influences and visionary thinkers and a lot of them have come up with great ideas and we are now putting that into a plan
Script: The Western Cape Government has been on the ground since the start assisting the municipality recover electricity and water supplies, and co-ordinating disaster plans. Later in the week President Jacob Zuma along with top government officials toured the disaster area.
Derek: What your impression
Zuma “Well this is a disaster it’s the effects of climate change and we have to be prepared for more disasters.”
Script: The insurance companies were the first on the ground says Insurance broker Albert Lombaard
Albert Lombaard “The companies so far is phenomenal they actually put up satellite stations in town and around town they flew in assessors and everyone working very everyone working pretty much 24 hours around the clock.
Script: Albert has processed 116 claims amounting to 500 million so far, and that for his practice alone. But many are under insured
Albert “ I have a got people who is actually under insured that’s their own choice they don’t believe in spending money to Insurance because it doesn’t happen in Knysna we are very protected here in actually here lots of people you think you live in a little bubble here
Script: The fire spread from Knysna to Plettenberg Bay overnight, destroying over 80 properties with some houses valued at R40 million - the claims bill is enormous
Link: “Most of the coverage the Cape Fires is focused on the homes burnt to the ground we tend to forget that 1000 of hectares of plantation that have been destroyed with the value of into 100’s of millions of rand
Script: Lawrence Polkinghorne, the CEO of MTO one of the largest plantation companies in this area, was on the fire line and is still overwhelmed when he thinks of his staffs bravery

Lawrence “Just watching people put their lives on the line for us you know we are a company we are a corporate we are a commercial business it’s just completely unbelievable the sense of commitment and dedication just containing it and the number of people saved and lives saved the homes you will never comprehend
Script One MTO fireman lost his life and 15 000 hectares of plantations, including a saw mill and processing plant were destroyed. 20 years of growth has been wiped out and the effects the economy will be felt for years to come,
Lawrence “Billions of rand worth of revenue is definitely impacted I mean you are taking all of that off the market so I mean it’s dire
Script: Fires are not uncommon in plantations in fact there were 64 fires in this area in December and not one hectare was lost. But wind gusts of up to 120 km an hour and after a long drought it was a perfect storm
Lawrence “Fires can jump anything from 100 meters up to 3 or 4 kilometres away so what you see are these long fires lines and the next thing behind you 3 kms away with 100 km wind is another new spot is another new fire so it’s just absolutely devastating
Script: They are trying to secure the jobs of the 1100 employees affected but many will have to be relocated.
Script: Extreme winds made this fire completely unmanageable striking over 300 kilometres along the garden route. Another fire flared up around Hankey and burnt towards the outskirts of Port Elizabeth hitting Woodridge school which has stood there since 1936, but miraculously all the children and staff escaped.
Upsound
Script: Paul Lynch has a son at the school and was fighting the fires till 3 am
UPsound from video of what’s burning
Paul “As an old boy to come back to your school and to watch it burn is just devastating but fortunately the community we have got here in PE the old original community have pulled together and as many people say we will rise out of the ashes and I firmly believe this school offers so much to the PE community that we have to rebuild it
Link: Fire fighters from across the country are exhausted after tackling one of the biggest blazes known to this coastline this week they have mainly been putting out flare-ups just preparing themselves for the next possible onslaught
Script: Andre De Ridder Chief Fire Officer for the Nelson Mandela Bay is still shocked by the intensity of the fires and has spent the week preparing for another outbreak
Andre “We are expecting extremely high gale force winds on we are making sure the embers are extinguished by that time otherwise we could have a repeat of some issues
Script: Joint operations meetings are happening daily with the farmers, Police, fire fighting units and all emergency personnel
Andre: “ Co- ordination with civic bodies is extremely important as a municipal service you never have enough fire fighters you never have enough staff you never have enough vehicles, so the civic organizations are vitally important to us and most certainly in the foreseeable future
Script: The first claims are already being paid out, and despite the devastation everyone we spoke to was hopeful.
Ella “I just have a good feeling about this whole disaster that has happened in Knysna everything will work itself out it will be better after this, Mom “hopefully hopefully for everybody”
